date.source: The federation's own recruitment post of 25 July 2003 bills the show as roughly a week away; its own results pointer of 7 August 2003 says the results are already posted. No exact card date is stated in any document this collection holds.

evidence.source: FSW Day of Reckoning 2003 (results pointer), 7 August 2003
evidence.note: The federation's own announcement that the results were posted; the results page itself was hosted externally (rspwf.com) and is not reachable under this collection's no-network rule.

evidence.source: GRANT-REVIEW: FSW Day of Reckoning PPV Review (2 of 3), 21 September 2003
evidence.note: The only surviving document to describe this card's own matches: a third-party critic's detailed recap and grading of the card's middle third. Parts 1 and 3 of the same review are not in the held record (only reply fragments quoting part 1 survive), so this record registers only the two matches this surviving fragment recaps; the rest of the card is not structured.

matches.stipulation: FSW Tag Team Championship, gauntlet match narrowing to a ladder match between the final two teams
matches.note: Per the surviving third-party recap: America's Least Wanted fell first to Scarlett/Bratzke without landing a move; Youth Gone Wild (Extasy named) then beat Scarlett/Bratzke; Heaven't Hunted fell to Youth Gone Wild next; the final two, Youth Gone Wild and the solo Mason Walker, then fought it out as a ladder match for the vacant belts. Walker and Extasy each grabbed one belt off the ladder as it fell; Walker was first up and about to claim the win outright when Youth Gone Wild's other, previously injured member recovered enough to chairshot him and grab the second belt, giving Youth Gone Wild the win and both titles.
A triple threat match; per the surviving third-party recap, John Shock pinned Johnny Malibu with a Yakuza kick to win.
